title: BetQL Review 2026: Prices, Refunds, Model Claims
description: BetQL review, checked 20 Nov 2026: weekly, monthly and annual prices, trial and refund terms, its own posted model records and 200 App Store reviews.
dek: A betting data app that rates bets from 1 to 5 stars with a computer model and sells public and sharp money reports. Web plans ran from $12.99 a week to $300 a year on 20 Nov 2026. It posts hand picked trend records rather than a full log of rated bets, and refunds are at the company's discretion.

short_answer: BetQL is a real, working product with a long paper trail. App Store reviews go back to 2018, its parent QL Gaming Group was bought in November 2020 by Entercom, the radio company now called Audacy, and today its terms list Skillbet Ltd in Malta as the operator. It has posted prices, apps on both major app stores and a support email. In that narrow sense it is legitimate. It sells a data tool and computer model ratings, not one handicapper's picks.

Whether following its star ratings makes money is a different question, and nothing we could open answers it. BetQL says each game is simulated 10,000 times and every bet gets 1 to 5 stars, but it publishes no full, dated log of every rated bet with the price and the time the rating was shown. What it does show is a rotating set of hand picked trend cards, such as "105-61-2 (63% win) on All 4-Star NFL bets". Several of those cards carry a headline win rate that does not match the record printed on the same card.

Buyer evidence is large but split. Of the 200 most recent App Store reviews we read, 105 gave five stars and 72 gave one star, and 64 of the five star reviews were posted in a three month burst in early 2021. Since 2022 the reviews are mostly negative, with repeated reports of losing five star picks, trouble cancelling and charges after a free trial. Treat BetQL as a research tool with an unproven model, use the free trial, and judge it on your own saved record.

guarantee: BetQL offers no guarantee tied to results. We found no promise of a free extension, credit or refund if the model's bets lose. On 20 Nov 2026 the subscribe page said "Monthly and annual plans start with a 3 Day Free Trial" and promised easy cancelling at any time. Weekly plans have no trial: the weekly view dropped the trial line and showed $12.99 due today. The checkbox for each plan says the charge "will auto-renew" every week, month or year "until cancelled".

The terms, last updated February 2025, say that if you give billing details for a trial "you will be automatically charged the applicable Subscription fees" when the trial ends unless you cancel, and that subscriptions "automatically renew under the exact same conditions". On refunds they say only that "Certain refund requests for Subscriptions may be considered by SKILLBET on a case-by-case basis." That is not a right to a refund. You cancel through the online account page or by contacting support.

The terms also send disputes to individual binding arbitration and waive class actions. You can opt out only by mailed, signed written notice postmarked within 30 days of accepting the terms. One detail to watch: on 7 Nov 2026 the annual view showed "$74.99 due today" next to the free trial banner, while on 20 Nov 2026 it showed "$0 due today". Check the amount on the checkout screen before you enter a card.

claims_note: How we checked. On 20 Nov 2026 the homepage showed 15 trend cards. We divided wins by wins plus losses on each card, ignoring pushes, and compared the result with the percentage printed on the card. All 15 printed percentages matched their own win loss counts after rounding; for example 35-21-1 is 62.5% and is shown as 63%. The headline above each card did not: cards were labelled "27% Win Rate", "35% Win Rate" or "0% Win Rate" while the record underneath showed 59% to 83%. We read these headlines as a display error, but a buyer cannot tell which number the site stands behind.

The cards are a filter, not a record. Each one is a slice the site picked because it is winning now: one team, one bet type, one star level, and windows that change from card to card (last 14 days, 30 days, 90 days, 365 days, or no window at all). Fifteen winning slices out of the thousands of bets the model rates say nothing about the rest. The dollar figures also show why win rate alone misleads: the Detroit Lions moneyline card wins 79% of the time but earned $473 on $2,800 risked, because favorites pay little.

One App Store reviewer in June 2023 quoted BetQL as saying that taking every five star basketball bet that season would have gone 356-300 for a $2,500 profit. If that figure is right, it is 54.3% winners and about a 3.8% return on 656 bets of $100. That is a thin edge, and we could not find the full log behind it.

The badges on the subscribe page do not match the stores. The page shows "4.8 App Store" while Apple showed 4.3 and Google Play showed 3.1. The page shows "200k+ active bettors" while the affiliate page speaks of 10,000 paying customers converted from 300,000 free users over an unstated 18 months.
record: BetQL does not publish a full, time stamped log of every model bet with the star rating, the line, the price and the post time, at least not on any page we could open without paying. The homepage says star ratings are updated "throughout the day" as lines move, so a buyer cannot check a rating after the fact unless they saved it at the time. A one star App Store reviewer in 2022 alleged that ratings were changed after games started; we could not test that.

What the seller publishes instead is the trend card carousel described above, profit figures per card in $100 units, and articles such as daily computer picks. The cards are recalculated as results come in, so the set we saw on 20 Nov 2026 will not be the set a reader sees next week.

Every BetQL page we opened carried the disclaimer that the site is "100% for entertainment purposes only". The terms add that it "does not involve real money betting or prizes". That sits beside a homepage pitch to find mispriced lines and an offers page full of real money sportsbook, prediction market and pick em sign up bonuses.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no BetQL model or BetQL expert is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how its ratings perform.
our_data.context: For scale: BetQL sells star ratings rather than a published win rate. Its homepage trend cards showed 59% to 83% winners on hand picked slices. On the Watchdog board on 20 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on BetQL comes mostly from the two app stores, plus a few Reddit threads. On 20 Nov 2026 we read all 200 reviews in Apple's most recent review feed, which runs from Nov 2018 to Sep 2026, and the top reviews on Google Play. Below is the pattern, then the individual posts and how much weight each can carry.

customers.text: We read 200 App Store reviews dated Nov 2018 to Sep 2026, the top Google Play reviews and the Reddit threads we could find from 2020 and 2021. The App Store set splits sharply: 105 five star, 6 four star, 6 three star, 11 two star and 72 one star. The positives cluster in time: 64 of the 105 five star reviews were posted between February and April 2021, the months after the Audacy purchase and the BetQL radio network launch, while no other year had more than 11. We cannot say why, and we do not suggest the reviews are fake, though two one star reviewers in 2019 and 2020 claimed the praise came from the company. Since 2022 the picture is mostly negative: of 28 reviews, 18 gave one star and 5 gave five stars. The same complaints repeat across years: five star picks losing (reviewers describe runs such as 1 and 18, 1 and 7 in three days, and 21 losses in 29 bets), trouble cancelling or reaching support (2019, 2020, 2021, 2024, 2025), charges after a free trial or out of season (2020, 2023), sportsbook promo rewards not delivered (2021, 2023), and public and sharp percentages that change after kickoff (2022, 2023). Positive reviewers praise the data and the price compared with handicappers and say they won, without records. Reddit posts were few and cool: one 2020 poster said it was not worth the money, and a 2021 thread split between a user who preps games with it and one who said the useful parts sit behind a paywall. No regulator, court or BBB complaint record turned up. Many independent buyers describing the same billing and support problems over several years is the kind of pattern worth weighing; the reports of losing picks are anecdotes from short runs.

customers.date: Featured reviews from Sep 2020 to Apr 2021; page checked 20 Nov 2026
customers.text: Apple's App Store listing showed 4.3 out of 5 from 1.8K ratings. The reviews shown on the page were positive and dated 2020 and 2021. One reviewer said the free 3 to 5 star bets seemed accurate and cheaper than paying a handicapper, but warned that ratings move a lot on late injury news. Several of these reviewers mentioned that other users had left negative reviews.

customers.date: Reviews from Feb 2020 to Oct 2023; page checked 20 Nov 2026
customers.text: The Google Play listing showed 3.1 stars from 1.38K reviews and 500K+ downloads, developer QL Gaming Group. The top reviews were about the app itself: an October 2023 review said a pop up ad would not close, and a February 2020 reviewer described log in problems, a web product that would not load and a price of $229.99 for three months. The developer replied to each and said the problems were fixed.

The subscribe page shows one testimonial credited to a social media handle described as a Pro subscriber, saying the sharp money tool has paid for itself many times over, plus a line that a staff member makes their living from BetQL data and now runs its YouTube channel. The affiliate page adds three short testimonials, one saying the writer was up 6K in a month. All are chosen and published by BetQL and cannot tell you what a typical buyer experiences.

Better Business Bureau searches for BetQL and for QL Gaming Group returned no business profile. We found no court case, regulator action or news report of a complaint against BetQL. Web searches of Sportsbook Review and Covers found no thread about BetQL we could open, and we did not use Trustpilot.
A five star App Store reviewer said BetQL helps find value on bets every day and claimed to be winning a lot more since starting to use it.
A five star reviewer called BetQL the best subscription they had bought and claimed to win around 8 of every 10 bets placed. That win rate is the reviewer's own claim and no record was shown.

A five star reviewer said that after trying many sites and cappers, BetQL was the most affordable with the best win rate they had seen from the 3 to 5 star bets, but warned that buyers have to accept losses along the way.
A one star reviewer said they had emailed four times in two weeks to cancel a membership and had not received a reply.
A one star reviewer said a free trial turned into a $50 charge without the cancellation notice BetQL says it sends, and that a refund request the next morning was refused as too late.

A one star reviewer claimed BetQL changes the star ratings on plays after games start, which they said makes its published accuracy figures unreliable. This is the reviewer's allegation, and we did not test it.
A one star reviewer asked why the app advertised 50% off the annual plan when no discount appeared at checkout.
A one star reviewer said three emails to support over ten days got no reply while the company kept trying to charge their card.

A one star reviewer said the five star model picks were not useful for making money, and mocked a BetQL message saying that every five star basketball bet that season would have gone 356-300 for a $2,500 profit, pointing out that this meant hundreds of losing bets along the way.
A one star reviewer said the five star bets went 1 and 7 over three days and told others not to waste their money.

A one star reviewer said the public and sharp betting percentages on a baseball game changed several minutes after the game began, flipping the side the reviewer had bet, and said they lost money relying on them.
A one star reviewer called the information useless and said BetQL kept charging for a sport after its season had ended.
A two star reviewer said betting the five star ratings almost every day for two weeks left them about $100 down.
A one star reviewer said they signed up at BetMGM with the BETQL promo code for a promised free year of VIP access, never received it, and got no answer to four emails sent from inside the app.

Dozens of five star reviewers in this period praised the public betting data, the best bets and the support staff, and several said they were winning or making money, for example by betting only four and five star ratings. None showed a record.
A one star reviewer said that after 22 days of using the ratings they were 1 and 18 and down 16 units.
A one star reviewer said 21 of their 29 five star bets had lost.
A one star reviewer said the paid picks were mostly wrong and that betting against the five star picks had worked somewhat better for them.
A one star reviewer said the app would charge them every week but they could not find any way to unsubscribe.

An early Google Play reviewer said $19.99 for two sports was too much, and that the app is not a prediction machine but a way to help decide on games you were already looking at, with a high win rate when used correctly.

In an r/sportsbook thread asking about betting advice apps, the original poster said they had used BetQL but it was not worth the money in their view, and that it pushed many advertisements for other apps.

An r/sportsbook thread asking whether anyone had a good experience with BetQL drew two replies. One said it was where they went to prep their games. The other said the main features sit behind a paywall and advised never paying for betting advice.

conflicts: BetQL runs a sportsbook offers page with sign up bonuses and promo codes, including the code BETQL for Betr and a promo code for Polymarket, plus offers from Dabble and a prediction market welcome offer. The homepage says it has "partnered with the top online sportsbooks and casinos in the US". Pages like this usually earn the site a fee when a reader signs up. That does not prove anything about the ratings, but it is a financial interest a buyer should know about.

BetQL also pays others to send it customers: its affiliate page offers "up to $100 CPA" or a "30% revenue share" for each referred subscriber and says the average customer spends about $250 over their lifetime. Reviews of BetQL on affiliate sites may be paid for in this way.

Ownership is not simple. In November 2020 Entercom and RADIO.COM announced they had acquired QL Gaming Group, the company behind BetQL, and in January 2021 a BetQL radio network launched. That network was renamed the BetMGM Network in February 2025 under a deal with the sportsbook BetMGM. On 20 Nov 2026 the BetQL terms named Skillbet Ltd, registered in Malta, as the operator (with the entity also written as SKILLBET, LLC), the Google Play developer was QL Gaming Group and the App Store seller was RotoQL, Inc. We could not confirm from a page we opened how these companies relate today.
strengths: Prices are posted for every web plan in weekly, monthly and annual views, and the trial, the amount due today and the auto renewal are stated before checkout.
Monthly and annual plans start with a 3 day free trial, and free rated bets and articles let a reader see the product before paying.
The method is described in plain terms: a simulation model, a 1 to 5 star scale, and separate public money, sharp money and line movement reports.
The trend cards print full win loss counts and dollar results, so a reader can do the arithmetic, as we did, rather than trust a bare percentage.
A long public history: a 2020 purchase by a large radio company, named companies in the terms, and apps on both stores where the developer answers complaints.
concerns: No full public record of rated bets, and ratings change during the day.
The trend cards are hand picked slices with shifting time windows, and their headline win rates contradicted the records printed beneath them on 20 Nov 2026.
No guarantee, and refunds are only at the company's discretion. Weekly plans have no trial and charge on day one.
Repeated buyer reports from 2019 to 2025 of trouble cancelling, slow support and charges after a trial.
The subscribe page claims a 4.8 App Store rating that Apple's own listing did not show.
The site earns from sportsbook and prediction market sign ups and pays affiliates per referred subscriber.
checklist: Ask for every rated bet from the last 12 months with the star rating, the line, the odds and the time it was posted. A carousel of hot trends is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 79% hit rate on heavy favorites can still earn very little, as the Lions card shows.
Read the terms for the words refund, credit and extension. Here the answer is no guarantee and refunds only at the company's discretion.
If you take the free trial, set a reminder for day two and cancel from the account page before it ends. Screenshot the cancellation.
Screenshot each rating the moment you bet it, with the line you can actually get, because the rating may change later.
Give any model or handicapper a few hundred picks before you call it a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real product with published prices, named operating companies, a 2020 purchase by Audacy on the record and apps on both app stores. We could not verify that its star ratings win over time, because it does not publish a full record of every rated bet, and the records it does show are hand picked trends.

On 20 Nov 2026 the website listed Starter (1 sport) at $12.99 a week, $30 a month or $75 a year, and All Access (all sports) at $24.99 a week, $70 a month or $300 a year. The iPhone app sold different plans through Apple, from a $4.99 day pass to $299.99 a year.

Its terms say refund requests "may be considered" case by case. Monthly and annual plans start with a 3 day free trial and charge automatically when it ends; weekly plans charge on day one. All plans auto renew until cancelled.
Is the BetQL free trial really free?

On 20 Nov 2026 the monthly and annual views showed $0 due today. Earlier in November the annual view showed $74.99 due today next to the same trial banner, and App Store reviewers in 2019, 2023 and 2024 described charges they did not expect or could not stop. Check the amount on the checkout screen and cancel before the trial ends if you do not want to pay.
What do BetQL's star ratings and trend records mean?

Each bet gets 1 to 5 stars from the model, and more stars are meant to mean a bigger edge. The trend cards on the homepage show how the model did on chosen slices, such as one team or one star level, over windows the site picks. They are not a full record, and some cards showed headline win rates that did not match their own numbers.
Not yet. No BetQL model or expert is matched to a Watchdog graded record in this edition. If that changes, this page will say so and show the record.
